name: Newfoundland and Labrador
summary: A white field with blue triangles at the hoist recalling the Union Flag, and at the fly a gold arrow and red trident-like shapes. Designed by the artist Christopher Pratt, it was adopted in 1980.
origin: Newfoundland used the Union Flag as its provincial flag until 1980. The painter Christopher Pratt designed a new flag, adopted on 28 May 1980 and first flown on 24 June, Discovery Day.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The sea, and the province's Commonwealth heritage.

symbols.name: Blue triangles
symbols.description: Triangles at the hoist resembling part of the Union Flag.

symbols.name: Two red triangles
symbols.meaning: The mainland (Labrador) and island (Newfoundland) parts of the province.

symbols.name: Gold arrow
symbols.description: An arrow pointing toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: Hope for a brighter future; together with the triangles it suggests a trident, for the fishing industry.

facts: Newfoundland was a separate Dominion until it joined Canada in 1949.
The 'Pink, White and Green' tricolour is a popular unofficial Newfoundland flag.
Christopher Pratt was a well-known Canadian painter.
clues: White with blue triangles at the hoist and a gold arrow with red triangles in the fly.
Designed by a painter in 1980 to replace the Union Flag.
Its fly shapes together suggest a trident.
